name: GA-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Clay Fuller renominated and running
Harris's large fundraising offset by heavy outside opposition spending
model.rationale: The seat's R+19 lean and a renominated Republican incumbent make this a Safe R race, and prediction markets agree at 96% for the GOP. Harris's $8.1 million in fundraising is notable but came with $446,000 in outside opposition spending and only $18,230 left on hand, limiting its impact in such a favorable Republican district.
model.watch: A major late scandal involving Fuller or a surge of Harris's spending into the final weeks could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
This northwest Georgia House seat is one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of R+19. Incumbent Clay Fuller was renominated and is seeking another term, giving Republicans both the incumbency advantage and the structural edge. Prediction markets price a Republican win at 96 percent, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive.

Democrat Shawn Harris has raised far more money than Fuller, about $8.1 million to $1.8 million, but has almost nothing left on hand and faces substantial outside opposition spending. Fuller retains outside support of his own. The fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican margin in the mid-to-high teens, with low but nonzero uncertainty given the absence of polling in the district.
